answer: Sealed hardware echo. Each agent identity is bound to a unique silicon die whose physical unclonable function answers a fresh challenge; the registry accepts one identity per die and records every reply so a cloned key cannot echo twice without collision. Enrollment requires presenting the die at a witnessed terminal, then surviving a cooling-cycle grove of random challenge rounds over months. An attacker must buy, physically hold, and operate one distinct chip per identity across that dune of elapsed time, paying fabrication plus custody cost per clone that never amortizes.
